INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport,
Tourism and Culture having authorized by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby
present this Two Hundred and Eighth Report on Action Taken by the Government on the
recommendations/observations of the Committee contained in its One Hundred Ninety Fifth Report
on the Demands for Grants (2013-14) of Ministry of Tourism.
2. One Hundred Ninety Fifth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee
on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented to the Parliament on the 3
rd May, 2013.
3. The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its One
Hundred Ninety Fifth Report were received from the Ministry of Tourism on the 6 th August, 2013.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on the 17 th December, 2013.
SITARAM YECHURY
NEW D ELHI; Chairman,
17th December, 2013 Department-related Parliamentary Standing
Agrahayana 26, 1935 (Saka) Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Tourism on
the observations/recommendations as contained in its One Hundred and Ninety Fifth Report on
Demands for Grants (2013-14) of the Ministry of Tourism, which was presented to both the
Houses of Parliament on 3
rd May, 2013.
2. The Action Taken Replies received from the Ministry in respect of all the observations/
recommendations contained in the Report have been categorized as follows:–
(i) Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Department:
Para Nos. 10, 11, 12, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 40, 50, 58, 61, 91, 100, 101, 102, 107,
108, 109, 118, 126, 130, 131, and 132 Total : 24
(ii) Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in
view of the Department replies:
Para Nos. 13, 54, 71, 79, 94, 100, 120, 125 and 134 Total : 9
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Department have not
been accepted by the Committee:
Para Nos . Nil
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry are
still awaited:
Para Nos. 25, 26, 27, 37, 38, 39, 52, 53, 64, 72, 95, 110, 119, 123, and 133 Total : 15
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of these recommendations/
observations, which have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be
furnished to it at the earliest.
On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each
item of Action taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee
contained in the One Hundred and Ninety Fifth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry and
recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the
succeeding paragraphs
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
4. The Committee notes that during Eleventh Plan period, the Ministry of Tourism could spend
Rs.4896 crore out of the Rs.4953 crore allocated at RE, which is almost 98% of the total
allocations. The Committee also notes that the Ministry of Tourism has sanctioned 1226 tourism
projects for an amount of Rs.4090 crore during the Eleventh Five Year Plan. But the Committee
was not informed about the completion of these projects or the current status of these projects.
It hopes that after sanctioning the projects and releasing the money, the Ministry of Tourism is
monitoring its implementation by the State Governments. It is learnt that the State Governments are
diverting these funds according to their own priority. The Committee recommends that the Ministry
should actively pursue each of these projects sanctioned to ensure that the sanctioned amount is
utilized in the prescribed manner for the approved project only.
(Para No. 10 of the 195
th Report)

2
Reply of the Government
5. The Ministry of Tourism monitors implementation of projects through Regional
Conferences, field inspections by the officers of State Governments/Union Territory
Administrations. The State Governments/Union Territory Administrations are also required to
periodically submit reports of the State Level Monitoring Committee to the Ministry of Tourism.
However, the pending projects are considered in the prioritization Meetings held with the State
Governments/Union Territory Administrations for the next Financial Year.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
6. The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
7. The Committee observes that under these schemes, Union territories appear to have been
neglected as the data shows that very few projects were sanctioned to them. For example,
Lakshadweep-1, Daman and Diu-1, Dadra and Nagar Haveli-3, and nothing for Andaman and
Nicobar Islands. The exceptions were Puducherry-20 and Chandigarh-11. If non receipt of the
proposal has been the reason, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of Tourism should
guide and encourage these union territories to submit viable projects so that they may also get the
fund allocations under these very important schemes. These areas have ample potential for tourism
development.
(Para No. 11 ibid)
Reply of the Government
8. Development and promotion of tourism destinations and products, including infrastructure
projects is primarily the responsibility of the respective State Governments/Union Territory
Administrations. The Ministry of Tourism only provides Central Financial Assistance (CFA) to the
projects prioritized and proposals received thereof from the State Government, subject to availability
of funds, inter-se priority and adherence to scheme guidelines.
9. The Ministry of Tourism, through prioritization and review meetings has been requesting  all
the Union Territory Administrations to submit proposals for various infrastructure projects.
However, the Union Territory Administrations of Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep
Islands have regularly stated that they are unable to take up projects due to Coastal Regulation Zone
regulations, clearances from the Ministry of Environment and Forests etc. Procuring material and
labour is another challenge and shortage of suitable experts/officers for planning projects is also
one of the major problems faced by Union Territories. The projects that have been sanctioned face
inordinate delays because of the afore-mentioned reasons. Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and
Diu have also been requested to send suitable project proposals.
10. Under the Twelfth plan the Ministry of Tourism has appointed State Level Project
Monitoring Agencies (SLPMA) to address some of the above problems particularly those related to
shortage of suitable experts. The SLPMAs would provide consultancy, make recommendations for
infrastructure projects to be taken up, and prepare DPRs. This would be done in consultation with
State Governments/Union Territory Administrations.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
11. The Committee observes that the constraints of the Andaman andNicobar Islands and
Lakshadweep Island Administrators are a genuine one. The Committee recommends that

3
the Ministry of Tourism need to look into the issues/difficulties in the coastal region as a
separate issue and tourism projects suitable to the topography of such regions should be
explored.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
12. The Committee also appreciates the NE-States on their eagerness in implementing tourism
projects during the Eleventh Plan period. All the NE-States have got good amount of allocations and
that Committee hopes that all these projects are being implemented earnestly and timely. This will
increase the tourist visits in this region which will improve their over all economic condition in the
coming years.
(Para No. 12  ibid )
Reply of the Government
13. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
14. The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
15. The Committee also observes that bigger States having immense potential for tourism
development, particularly pilgrimage, wild life and niche tourism, have not had commensurate
projects/funds under these schemes. The Committee recommends that more attention should be
given during Twelfth Plan to those States which were yet to exploit their potential for tourism
development.
(Para No. 13 ibid)
Reply of the Government
16. The Ministry of Tourism has appointed a National Level Consultant to identify major tourist
circuits in the country except North-Eastern States and they have  identified integrated tourism
circuits, Rural Tourism Cluster and Tourism Parks, in consultation with the respective State
Governments. For identification/development of Tourism Circuits in the North – East Region (NER)
a study has been conducted by Tata Consultancy Services commissioned by North-Eastern Council,
Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
17. The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
18. This Committee has always been arguing the case of Ministry of Tourism for enhanced
allocations every year during the examination of its Demands for Grants. The Planning
Commission, however, appears to have been reluctant to do so for reasons best known to it.
Normally, it does not give any reason for this to a Ministry. During current year also, only
Rs.1282.00 crore has been allocated to the Ministry against a projected demand of Rs.1773.79
crore. The Committee, keeping in view the various targets fixed for development and promotion
of tourism infrastructure, creating skilled and trained manpower, exploring new tourism projects
etc., reiterates its recommendation for providing additional funds to the Ministry of Tourism so that

4
the ideal of linking tourism with employment generation and poverty alleviation could be achieved
in reality.
(Para No. 20 ibid)
Reply of the Government
19. The Ministry of Tourism agrees with the recommendation of the Committee for enhancing
the allocation under Plan Schemes.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
20. The Committee recommends to convey its sentiments in this regard to the Planning
Commission, Ministry of Finance for necessary action.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
21. The Committee notes that during the Eleventh Plan period, right from the opening years,
the spending had remained more than 98%. However, in the opening year (2012-13) of the Twelfth
Plan, the spending patterns had not been so. The BE 2012-13 stood at Rs.1210 crore which was
reduced at the RE to Rs.950 crore. But only Rs.724.34 crore could be spent upto February, 2013.
If this spending is analyzed on the basis of the BE allocation of Rs.1210 crore during the period,
it forms only 60% of it. The Committee feels that there are failures on the part of the Ministry
in dealing with Plan Schemes whatever be the adverse policy changes. The Ministry should have
taken up the matter at the appropriate Governmental levels, rather than blaming the system. The
Committee recommends that Ministry of Tourism needs to be more proactive and work as
facilitator for implementation of its schemes.
(Para No. 21 ibid)
Reply of the Government
22. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted to be more proactive and work as
facilitator for implementation of its schemes.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
23. The Committee feels that merely noting its concerns is not enough, the Ministry has
to list out efforts made in this regard.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
24. The Committee notes that the Ministry has not projected their achievement in measurable
terms by providing required information in quantified and comparable format to the Committee.
That would have helped the Committee to understand and appreciate the real problems before the
Ministry and concretize its opinion accordingly. Next time the Committee would like to have
information in user friendly format for its purpose.
(Para No. 22 ibid)
Reply of the Government
25. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for taking suitable steps in this
regard.

5
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
26. The Committee would like to see a format in which the Ministry proposes to send
information, figures etc. for examining its Demands for Grants showing financial and
physical performance in respect of last three years including those proposed for the coming
Financial Year.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
27. The Committee also notes that some of the schemes such as incentives to accommodation,
assistance to large revenue generating projects, creation of land banks, etc. are languishing for
many years. The Committee recommends that these schemes may be reviewed so that it may
accomplish its targets.
(Para No. 23 ibid )
Reply of the Government
28. The proposal for continuation of scheme ‘Incentives Scheme for Budget Hotels’ to provide
subsidy to private sector for augmenting the budget accommodation in the categories of 1, 2 and
3 star hotels was discussed with the Planning Commission. The Planning Commission was of the
view that the Ministry of Tourism need not pursue this scheme. As regards other schemes, the
recommendation of the Committee has been noted for taking suitable action.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
29. The Committee would like to know “suitable action” taken by the Ministry of
Tourism in respect of other schemes as stated in their reply above.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
30. The Committee observes that the strict guidelines on adherence to the utilization certificate
of each projects and further allocation of funds strictly thereafter has been able to bring some
accountability and discipline in the spending pattern of the Ministry. However, the Committee is of
the opinion that such measures should be based on practical consideration as the infrastructure
projects are required to get various sanctions/clearances from so many agencies under different
Ministries. Usually, the projects, involving land acquisition and environment clearance are the most
time consuming. Therefore, keeping all these matters in mind, if the interpretation of rules/
guidelines on fund disbursement scheme has posed any problem ·to the Ministries, it should be
taken up at appropriate levels and resolved as soon as possible.
(Para No. 24 ibid)
Reply of the Government
31. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for implementation.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
32. The Committee would like to know efforts being made for implementation of the
above recommendation.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
33. The Committee notes that the Twelfth Plan has given emphasis to rural tourism and
projected tourism as a tool to reduce poverty. The Committee, however, finds no special schemes

6
or efforts to promote the rural tourism or spread the idea of tourism as a mass activity. The
Committee notes in the Budget 2013-14, just routine programmes which are going on for the last
so many years.
(Para No. 25 ibid)
Reply of the Government
34. The Ministry of Tourism implements the scheme “Product/Infrastructure Development for
Destinations and Circuits” which also includes the provision for the development of rural projects.
The said Scheme is under revision for Twelfth Plan and the Ministry of Tourism has proposed to
develop ‘Rural Tourism Cluster’ instead of standalone villages.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
35. Again the Committee feels that the Ministry has given a sketchy reply. Therefore,
the Committee may be appraised on the details of the scheme.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
36. The Committee is also of the view that the plans and programmes of the Ministry of
Tourism should be aimed at positioning tourism as a major contributor of economic growth and
harness its direct and multiplier effects for employment and poverty eradication in an
environmentally sustainable manner. The schemes taken up by the Ministry should be aimed at
enhancing employment in the activities relating to tourism sector as well as at fostering economic
integration through developing linkages with other sectors.
(Para No. 26 ibid)
Reply of the Government
37. During Twelfth Five year Plan the Ministry of Tourism has proposed a strategy for pro-
poor tourism. The Planning Commission has also emphasized on the need to adopt a “pro-poor
tourism” approach aimed at increasing the net benefits to the poor from tourism and ensure that
tourism growth contributes to poverty reduction. This strategy will also lead to the growth of
employment in the country.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
38. The ‘pro-poor tourism’ sounds interesting to the Committee. It would like to have
a note on it spelling out clearly its components, strategy to be adopted and its possible
implications to the poor.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
39. The Committee further recommends that with the aim to achieve socio-economic development
in rural areas which have core competence in arts, crafts, heritage etc., the Ministry of Tourism
should provide assistance for development of tourism infrastructure and capacity building of rural
inhabitants in the States. The Ministry need to pursue with the State Governments for completion of
rural tourism projects sanctioned in a particular financial year within a fixed time-frame.
(Para No. 27 ibid)
Reply of the Government
40. The Ministry of Tourism has been providing Central Financial Assistance (CFA) to States/

7
Union Territories for rural tourism projects. The State/UT Governments are regularly pursued  for
completion of sanctioned projects within prescribed time limit.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
41. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee desires to know the response from
State Governments/UTs in this regard and accordingly a consolidated Status report may be
furnished.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
42. The Committee notes that allocations for PIDDC scheme are getting reduced as compared
to allocations made during 2011-12 and 2012-13. The Committee also notes that current year
allocation stands further reduced at Rs.400 crore. The Committee thus finds a regular reduction
in allocation from the 2011-12 onwards. A re-interpretation of the guidelines for funds disbursal in
this regard was given as the reason. The Ministry of Finance regulations provides that spending
pattern of the first quarter is criteria for getting eligible for subsequent allocations on various
schemes of the States. The Committee observes that these guidelines may have adverse impact on
other projects also and in such a case no scheme could be properly implemented by the States.
The Committee recommends that the utilization certificates may be obtained scheme/project-wise.
If a particularly scheme/project is lagging behind in its execution, it should not be a reason to deny
fund to the other schemes/projects of the State. The Committee recommends that the guidelines
on the utilization certificates may be reviewed by the Ministry of Finance so that the proposed
projects may not be affected by the bottlenecks in the fund allocation norms.
(Para No. 37 ibid)
Reply of the Government
43. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. The matter will be taken up with
the Ministry of Finance regarding the fund allocation norms so that the proposed projects are not
affected.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
44. The Committee would like to know the stand taken by Ministry of Finance in this
regard.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
45. The Committee observes that even though the rural tourism scheme was started in the year
2002-03, the scheme has not made much progress so far. Only 186 projects have been sanctioned
since the inception of the scheme. The completion status is less than 50% as only 90 projects out
of 186 have been completed during a decade i.e. 2002-2012. Now the scheme has been replaced
with Rural Tourism Cluster scheme. The Committee observes that undue delay in implementing the
scheme is not acceptable. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Tourism may set the
guidelines in such a way that the scheme may yield results at the earliest.
(Para No. 38 ibid)
46. The Committee recommends that Ministry of Tourism should ensure convergence of
resources and expertise through coordinated efforts with State/UT Governments and stakeholders
for an integrated and intensive development of tourism infrastructure in the country through careful
planning and execution while giving importance for improvement in accessibility, environmental and
other aspects.The Committee recommends that Ministry of Tourism should ensure convergence of

8
resources and expertise through coordinated efforts with State/UT Governments and stakeholders
for an integrated and intensive development of tourism infrastructure in the country through careful
planning and execution while giving importance for improvement in accessibility, environmental and
other aspects.
(Para No. 39 ibid)
Reply of the Government
47. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
48. The Committee desires to know the follow up action taken in this regard.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
49. The Committee notes that some projects identified in the years 2008-09, 2009-10 or 2010-11
are yet to take off like Aurangabad destinations of Maharashtra, Eco and Adventure circuit,
Arunachal Pradesh, Mubarak Mandi Heritage, Jammu and Kashmir etc. as no fund allocations have
been made for these so far. The Committee recommends that the concerned State Governments
may be encouraged to take the follow-up actions in these regards and the funds may be granted
in each case at the earliest.
(Para No. 40 ibid)
Reply of the Government
50. The Ministry of Tourism has sanctioned the project – Development of Aurangabad as a
Mega Destination in the year 2012-13 for a total Central Financial Assistance (CFA) of Rs.2343.20
lakh with release of Rs.117.16 lakh to the Government of Maharashtra so that the State
Government can initiate the works pertaining to the project. In Arunachal Pradesh one adventure
tourism project ‘Development of Adventure Tourism Campaign Destination site at Jottee Poma
River’ sanctioned in 2008-09 and one eco-tourism project ‘Construction of Eco-Tourism at Tego
Gamlin Village, West Siang’ sanctioned in 2009-10 have been completed with CFA of Rs.387.05
lakh and Rs.370.65 lakh respectively. As far as Jammu and Kashmir is concerned, one project for
Conservation/Restoration of Mubarak Mandi Heritage Complex, Jammu as a Mega Tourist
Destination has been sanctioned in 2012-13 with CFA of Rs.1691.57 lakh and Rs.338.31 lakh have
been released as first installments.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
51. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee is happy to know about the new
initiatives undertaken during the financial year 2013-14.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
52. The Committee notes that there was about one third cut in the allocations during the RE
stage for Domestic Campaign but even then it could not be utilized properly during 2012-13. The
spending up to February 2013 was Rs.55.62 crore out of the RE amount of Rs.65 crore. The
Committee feels the revision of rates and DA VP guidelines are not convincing reasons for this. The
Committee feels that Ministry should have been more careful about this. The Committee also feels
that the projects proposed by the Ministry need to be innovative, interactive, and educative using
mostly the print and electronic media. The Committee appreciates the work done at the Delhi and

9
Mumbai airports. The schools and colleges throughout India can also be involved to spread
awareness about tourism. The school children may be given incentives to undertake tours and
excursions by the Ministry of Tourism which may ignite awareness of children and ultimately
results in promotion of tourism. The Ministry of Tourism should come forward with innovative
campaign strategies on these lines. The Committee also recommends that the State Governments
may be guided and assisted in marketing the tourist destinations and circuits in a particular State
as the Centre is not marketing the State destinations directly.
(Para No. 50 ibid)
Reply of the Government
53. The recommendation of the Committee to involve schools and colleges for spreading
awareness about tourism has been noted for inclusion in the future. Further, development and
promotion of tourism, including new tourism spots, is primarily the responsibility of the State
Governments/Union Territory Administrations.
54. The Ministry of Tourism provides financial assistance to State Governments and Union
Territory Administrations for production of publicity material. The Ministry of Tourism also
provides financial assistance to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations for
tourism projects based on proposals, received from them which are complete in all respects as
per the Scheme Guidelines, inter-se -priority and subject to availability of funds. Under the
Scheme ‘Product/Infrastructure Development for Destinations and Circuits’, the Ministry of
Tourism also provides Central Financial Assistance for last mile connectivity to the tourism
destinations.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
55. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Tourism being the nodal agency connecting
all the institutions and State Governments in tourism promotion, they may also share their
memorable experiences with other States, so that they can also follow the pattern.
Therefore, rather than a monitoring agency, it can be a guide to others for getting similar
efforts converted to success stories in future.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
56. The Committee feels that the initiatives of “Clean India Campaign” is a good idea but the
manner in which it has been proposed to be implemented leaves much to be desired. As has
happened in the case of National Culture Fund (NCF), under Ministry of Culture, this campaign
also may not get desired response from the PSU, etc. We understand that the desired activity
perhaps has not been recognized as an activity under Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). And
if it is so, the Ministry of Tourism should together with Ministry of Culture, pursue this matter
with the concerned Ministries for this purpose. The Committee expresses its doubt about the
success of such a campaign in the existing form.
(Para No. 52 ibid)
Reply of the Government
57. The Ministry of Tourism has launched ‘Campaign Clean India’ to bring about an acceptable
level of cleanliness at important tourist destinations. This campaign is to be sustained through
adoption and involvement of private and public sector stakeholders as part of their Corporate Social
Responsibility (CSR). The campaign is not restricted to upkeep and cleanliness only. The adopters
have taken holistic approach in adopting monuments for overall up-gradation including components

10
such as restoration, preservation, beautification, cleanliness and maintenance of the monuments and
its surroundings.

Nagaland only. Citizens of other States require ILP for visiting these three States. However, certain
class of people like the Central Government and State Government employees who possess valid
Identity Cards as proof of their being Government servants, are exempted from permits while
visiting these States.
141. The ILP is issued by State Government officials and MHA is not consulted in the matter.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
142. The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
143. The Committee recommends for more cruise tourism projects at the viable states on the
lines of the initiative taken in Cochin Port. All the Major Ports, especially the Mormugao Port has

22
immense potential of cruise tourism which needs to be explored by the Ministry of Tourism for
development.
(Para No. 123 ibid)
Reply of the Government
144. The Steering Committee on Cruise Tourism has identified the ports of Chennai, Cochin,
New Mangalore, Mormugao and Mumbai for development of Cruise Tourism.
145. Under the Guidelines for implementing Scheme for Assistance to Central agencies for
Tourism Infrastructure Development, the Ministry of Tourism provides financial assistance to the
ports for development of Cruise Tourism related infrastructure.
146. During 2012-13, the Ministry of Tourism has sanctioned an amount of Rs.2243.32 lakh to
Cochin Port Trust for Development of dedicated cruise berthing facilities at Cochin Port and an
amount of Rs.1724.66 lakh to Chennai Port Trust for developing Cruise Passenger Facility Centre
in the existing passenger terminal at Chennai Port.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
147. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee desires to know the facilities/
services available to the tourists in the above two cases.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
148. The Committee notes the various measures taken in the Adventure tourism. The Committee
also recommends that adequate trained people should be deputed in all the adventure spots to
monitor the participants and for rescue operations if required.
(Para No. 125 ibid)
Reply of the Government
149. Development and promotion of tourism is primarily the responsibility of State Governments/
UT Administrations concerned. Training and provision of safety equipment for various activities for
adventure tourism including safety-precautionary measures to prevent any untoward incidents, are
under the purview of the concerned State Governments/UT Administrations. The Ministry of Tourism,
under its ‘Hunar Se Rozgar Tak’ Scheme assists the State Governments/UT Administrations,
recognized adventure institutes for organizing Training/Skill Development Programmes for the
unemployed youth as Adventure Travel Guides, Eco Rural Guides, River Rafting Guides etc.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
150. The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
151. The Committee feels that there is lot of potential in all these new tourism products like
Cruise, Adventure, Medical, Wellness, Golf, Polo, Meetings, Incentives Conferences and Exhibitions
(MICE), Eco-tourism and Film Tourism. The Ministry of Tourism should work on a detailed guide
map on all these areas.
Reply of the Government
152. The Ministry of Tourism has taken the initiative of identifying, developing and promoting

23
various niche products of the tourism to overcome the aspect of ‘seasonality’ to promote India as
a 365 day destination, attract tourists with specific interests and to ensure repeat visits for the
unique products in which India has competitive advantage. The niche products identified by the
Ministry of Tourism for development and promotion inter-alia, include Cruise, Adventure, Medical,
Wellness, Golf, Polo, Meetings, Incentives Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE), Eco-tourism and
Film Tourism.
153. The production of guide maps/brochure and tourist literature for various products including
the ‘Niche Tourism’ Products is an ongoing process in the Ministry and the recommendation of
the Committee is noted for compliance.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
154. The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
155. The Committee observes that safety and security is equally important, if not more, for the
growth of tourism sector. The Committee is concerned about the recent incidents of attacks on
tourists at different parts of the country. In addition to this, the Committee noticed that even
though safety guidelines are in place, these are less enforced and the authorities are negligent
towards these aspects until there are some incidents. All the State Governments, therefore, may be
persuaded/helped to set up tourism Police and prevent touts and goons from various tourist
destinations, airports, railway stations, etc. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the safety
measures should be strictly implemented and monitored at the different levels. The 24x7 infoline
in foreign languages is a welcome step up to attract the tourists. However, the Ministry should
ensure that the people who are manning it are capable and the service is available at ease. It should
assist the tourists, whenever they want.  (Para No.130 ibid)
Reply of the Government
156. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance.
1. In order to ensure safety and security of tourists, including foreign tourists, the
Ministry of Tourism has advised all the State Governments/Union Territory
Administrations to deploy Tourist Police in the States/Union Territories. The State
Governments/Union Territory Administrations of Andhra Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka,
Kerala, Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttar Pradesh,
Delhi, Punjab, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha have deployed Tourist Police, in one form
or the other.
2. Further, the guidelines for formation of Tourist Facilitation and Security Organisation
comprising Ex-servicemen formulated by the Ministry of Tourism in consultation with the
Ministry of Defence, Home and Directorate General of Re-settlements have been forwarded
to the State Governments/Union Territory Administrations for necessary action.
3. In addition, the Ministry of Tourism along with stakeholders has adopted the ‘Code of
Conduct for Safe and Honourable Tourism’ which is a set of guidelines to encourage tourism
activities to be undertaken with respect to basic rights like dignity, safety and freedom from
exploitation of both tourist and local residents, in particular, women and children.
4. In the wake of unfortunate incidents involving foreign tourists, the Ministry of Tourism
has posted its advisory on its website 
www.incredibleindia.or g indicating that India
remains a safe destination for international tourists including women.

24
5. Further, the Ministry of Tourism has also written to all the Chief Secretaries of the
State Governments and Union Territory Administrations to take immediate effective
steps for ensuring conducive and friendly environment for all tourists. They have also
been requested to publicize the steps being taken/proposed to be taken to increase the
sense of security amongst the present/prospective visitors and also to counter the
negative publicity.
6. In order to further emphasise the need for ensuring safety and security of tourists in
general and esteemed lady guests in particular, Hon’ble Minister of State for Tourism
(Independent Charge) has written personally to all the Chief Ministers of States and
Union Territory Administrators.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
157. The Committee notes the various steps the Government has taken for the safety and
security of the tourists.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
158. The Committee observes that the Tourism Ministry is mainly a fund-disbursing agency.
More than 90 per cent of its Plan allocation every year goes to four schemes relating to
infrastructure development, training assistance to institutes and publicity - overseas and domestic.
Once these funds are released, it seems it is left with the State Governments and Union territories
to utilise them. Nowhere is it reflected how the Ministry is monitoring the utilisation of these funds
and how they get feedback on whether the States and Union territories are actually utilising these
funds for the purpose for these funds have been allocated. The Committee desires to know whether
there is any robust mechanism at different levels to coordinate these various aspects.
(Para No. 131 ibid)
Reply of the Government
159. The Ministry of Tourism monitors implementation of projects through Regional
Conferences, field inspections by the officers of State Governments/Union Territory
Administrations. State Governments/Union Territory Administrations are also required to periodically
submit reports of the State Level Monitoring Committee to the Ministry of Tourism.  The field
offices of MoT are also assigned inspections and the Ministry deputes its officers also to inspect
the projects, from time to time.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
160. The Committee recommends for further strengthening of the prevailing system in
order to get better performance over all. A review mechanism on the present system may
also be worked out.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
161. The Committee observes that sky rocketing of airfares and lack of Government control over
it has recently affected the domestic tourist movement in the country. The Committee also observes
that higher user fee and ATF surcharges have eventually made the air traffic journey un-affordable
to many. The DGCA has taken some steps in this regard. The Committee however, recommends
that a more regular and strict watch on predatory airfares being resorted by the airlines needs to
done to prevent unreasonable airfares especially during the peak seasons.
(Para No. 132 ibid)

25
Reply of the Government
162. The recommendation of the Committee has been noted for compliance. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
163. The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
164. The Committee also observes that the rail travellers are facing problems due to shabby
coaches which are usually unclean with rodents roaming freely. The toilets are very dirty and are
seldom cleansed during the journey. Beggar menace and under quality food served are other areas
to be immediately attended. All these problems have made the train journey a nightmare for most
of the travellers and the tourists in particular. The Committee recommends that Ministry of Tourism
may take up the matter with Railway Board so that the train journey may be made attractive and
comfortable to the tourists.
(Para No. 133 ibid)
Reply of the Government
165. Prime Minister’s  Office has constituted an Inter Ministerial Coordination Committee for
Tourism Sector (IMCCTS) under the Chairmanship of the Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister
to facilitate the resolution of inter-ministerial issues involved in the development of tourism in the
country, as well as issues raised by Industry Associations in the tourism sector. The Ministry of
Tourism takes up all such issues through this Committee with the Ministry of Railways.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
166. The Committee desires to know the follow up action in this regard.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
167. The Committee observes that we are not utilizing the full potential of tourism in India. We
always feel very sad about the fact that, probably, there is no country like ours that has snow,
hills to seas and beaches, adventure tourism, wildlife tourism, medical tourism, etc., within the
country. India has such a wide variety and destination. In spite of that, the confidence does not
seem to come that we are able to actually reach anyway close to using our potential.
(Para No. 134 ibid)
Reply of the Government
168. The Ministry of Tourism has a target to increase India’s share of International Tourist
arrivals to at least 1% by the end of Twelfth Plan and provide adequate facilities for domestic
tourism to sustain the growth of 12.16% during Twelfth Plan period.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
169. The Committee hopes that the decline in rupee value may bring more international
tourists to the country as a trip to India is cheaper than before.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman, Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Transport,
Tourism and Culture, having been authorised by the Committee to present on its behalf, do hereby
present this Two Hundred and Ninth Report on “Action Taken Replies by the Ministry of Civil
Aviation on the observations/recommendations as contained in its One Hundred and Ninety First
Report on Demands for Grants (2013-14) of the Ministry of Civil Aviation”.

Committee on Transport, Tourism and Culture was presented on the 3
rd May, 2013 to the
Parliament.
3. The Action Taken Replies on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its One
Hundred and Ninety First Report was received from the Ministry of Civil Aviation on 1 st October, 2013.
4. The Committee considered and adopted the Report in its meeting held on the
17th December, 2013.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Civil Aviation
on the observations/recommendations as contained in its One Hundred and Ninety First Report on
Demands for Grants (2013-14) of the Ministry of Civil Aviation, which was presented to both the
Houses of Parliament on 3
rd May, 2013.
2. The Action Taken Replies received from the Ministry in respect of all the observations/
recommendations contained in the Report have been categorized as follows:–
(i) Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Department:
Para Nos. 7, 10, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 47, 61, 62, 63, 73, 76, 82, 88, 91, 93,
101 and 103
(ii) Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view
of the Department replies:
Nil. 69, 80, 94 and 102
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Department have not
been accepted by the Committee:
Para Nos. 87, 99 and 100
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry are still
awaited:
Para Nos. 10, 37, 38, 88, 89, 90 and 92
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of these recommendations/
observations, which have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be
furnished to it at the earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each
item of Action taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee
contained in the One Hundred and Ninety First Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry and
recommendations/observations of the Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the
succeeding paragraphs
ANNUAL PLAN 2012-13
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
5. The Committee finds that the spending pattern of Plan funds has been poor during
2012-13 which needs a lot of improvement. The Committee hopes that the Ministry of Civil
Aviation will impress the concerned organizations/undertakings to spend the allocated fund with
proper planning and coordination with respective stakeholders. The Committee notes that except the
investment in Air India, all other organizations were allocated substantially reduced allocations at RE
stage which also could not be optimally utilized. The Committee feels that reduction of funds at
RE stage does not augur well for the much beleaguered aviation sector. Most of these under-
utilizations have been mainly due to finalization of schemes. The Committee expresses dismay over
non-finalization of building plan for BCAS and DGCA that are pending for so many years. Slow

2
progress in case of NER projects is a cause of concern to the Committee. The Committee
recommends the Ministry to take necessary steps urgently to finalize/approve these Plan schemes
at the earliest to spend the allocated funds during the current year.
(Recommendation at Para 7 of 191
st Report)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
6. Air India has utilized the entire amount of budgetary resources which were allocated to
them i.e. Rs.6,000 crores by way of Equity Infusion. There has been no under-utilisation of the
allocated funds.
7. AAI has spent an amount of Rs.145.35 crore in 2012-13 which is around 99% of the RE
2012-13 allocation of Rs.147 crore. However, an amount of Rs.59.29 crores only could be released
in 2012-13 due to expenditure ceiling for the last quarter/month of the financial year.
8. AAI is in readiness to take up the construction work of DGCA and BCAS Headquarter
buildings. However, the work is held up due to resumption of Safdarjung Airport land unilaterally
by the Ministry of Urban Development and declaring it as green recreational area. The efforts of
this Ministry to get back the Safdarjung Airport land did not succeed and the matter has been
referred to the Cabinet Secretariat for a decision. The work on DGCA and BCAS building at other
locations viz. Amritsar, Ahmedabad, Bhubaneswar, Guwahati and Mumbai has been awarded and
construction activities commenced at these locations.
9. The Airports Authority of India (AAI) has spent an amount Rs.6.12 crore in 2012-13 against
the RE 2012-13 allocaton of Rs.7.62 crore for the development of airport infrastructure in the
North East. However, funds could not be released in 2012-13 due to expenditure ceiling for the
last quarter/month of the financial year.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
10. The details of the meetings undertaken with the Ministry of Urban Development as
regards the construction work of DGCA and BCAS Headquarters buildings may also be
informed to the Committee. The Committee recommends that matter may be taken up
expeditiously. The Committee further recommends that Ministry should pursue the removal
of restrictions of 33% ceiling of expenditure for the last quarter with the Ministry of
Finance seriously. The ceiling on spending in last quarter ultimately results in under-
utilization of funds and delay in execution of infrastructure projects.
ANNUAL PLAN 2013-2014
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
11. The Committee notes that the Ministry of Civil Aviation was able to get only 56% of the
projected plan allocations for the current fiscal. The Committee feels that such inadequate allocation
will definitely hamper progress of ongoing infrastructure projects and other aviation related
programmes. The Committee hopes that the Ministry will expedite the approval of various Schemes
and persuade Planning Commission for allocation of more funds at RE stage. The Committee also
hopes that the allocated funds will be utilized judiciously to avoid any reduced allocation at RE
stage.
(Para 10 of ibid)

14. AAI has submitted an additional demand of Rs.462.21 crore (2013-14) for carrying out

FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE

GROUND HANDLING SBU
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
16. The Committee notes that despite many labour unrests witnessed during the last year, the
national carrier was able to improve its performance notably both financially and operationally. It
recorded positive EBITDA of Rs.19 crores during the year 2012-13 as against a negative EBITDA
of Rs.2237 crores during the year 2011-12. Air India’s on-time performance was 84.8 % in the
case of domestic sector and 74 % for international sector as against the turnaround plan
benchmark of 85%. The passenger load factor of Air India was 72% as against the target under
turnaround plan of 69.5%. The turnaround plan benchmark on yield per kilometer was 3.53, against
which Air India achieved 3.76.
(Para 36 of ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
17. Agreed. For the year 2013-14, EBITDA of more than Rs.1000.00 crores has been budgeted.
There has also been an improvement in the physical performance in terms of ‘On Time
Performance, Load Factor etc.’.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
18. The Committee hopes that the national carrier will improve its performance in the
current fiscal both in respect of financial and physical aspects.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
19. The Committee finds that Air India was able to get Rs.5000 crores as against the
requirement of Rs.8574. The Committee finds that as part of the FRP and as approved by the
Cabinet, the Government of India had given a commitment to infuse the Equity as per the FRP.
Any delay or shortfall in the infusion of the equity would adversely affect the implementation of
Turn Around Plan and FRP, since Air India would be compelled to borrow short term loans from
Banks in order to bridge the equity gap which would entail payment of interest, which may
adversely affect the profitability of the company. In fact, one of the conditions under which, the
regulator (RBI) and the consortium of Banks supported the FRP, entails timely equity support to
Air India by Government of India.
(Para 37 of ibid)

4
20. The Committee feels that since Air India has started achieving the milestones as prescribed
in the TAP during the last year, further allocation of Rs.3574 crores as equity infusion will help
the national carrier to implement the turnaround plan smoothly and carry forward the improved
performance in the coming years also. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government
should provide the promised equity infusion which has been accumulated without any interruption
during the course of the financial year.
(Para 38 of ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
21. Ministry is taking up with Department of Expenditure for grant of additional budget of
Rs.3574.00 crores at RE-2013-14 stage.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
22. The Committee desires that it may be appraised on the reply of the Ministry of
Finance and Planning Commission on the request of the Ministry for additional demand of
funds for infusion of equity in Air India.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
23. The Committee feels that Air India with its wide range of aircraft in its kitty should expand
its operations beyond metro cities. Since majority of the non-metro airports have been modernized/
developed by Airports Authority of India, the national carrier should make efforts to penetrate those
unexplored markets. When the private carriers are in a position to offer air services to Tier-II and
Tier-III cities, Air India should explore offering its services to such cities using smaller aircrafts.
The Committee still feels that Air India’s entry into LCC segment will definitely strengthen its
business. The Committee recommends that the Air India should try to provide better service and
products to the passengers which have lot of scope for improvement.
(Para 39 of ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
24. Air India is trying to connect non-metro airports through its operations as well as through
that of its subsidiary :Alliance Air. It is proposed to replace 19, A320 aircraft with brand new ones
which would be in an all economy configuration. This would provide the necessary capacity to
provide connectivity to the Tier II and Tier III cities as well as satisfy the requirement of the LCC
segment of the domestic market. Air India would certainly endeavor to provide better services to
its passengers in the coming years.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
25. The Committee notes the reply and hopes that with the replacement of old A320
aircraft, the national carrier can expand its connectivity beyond metro cities in the coming
years.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
26. The Committee also hopes that Air India’s entry into ground handling operations will add
much needed financial fillip for the company. The Committee notes that process of operationalising
the MRO SBU is going on in a snail’s pace and the Government and the Air India do not appear

5
to be taking adequate initiatives to speed up the process. The Committee is confident that the MRO
SBU and the Ground handling activity of AIATSL, if planned and executed properly, can bring lot
of revenue to Air India. The Committee recommends that the Government should, if need be, make
necessary policy changes to enable these two agencies to function on proper business and
commercial prudence. The Committee notes significant headway in implementing the human
resources merger programmes. The Committee recommends that all the outstanding issues must be
settled as early as possible to enable Air India to function as a single entity.
(Para 40 of ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
27. The process of operationalization of the subsidiary companies was slow during the year
2011-12 mainly on account of the requirement of necessary approvals. After receiving the Cabinet
approval in September 2012, Air India went ahead with the operationalisation of the subsidiary
companies. However, the Unions of Air India challenged the same before the Mumbai High Court.
After a series of hearings, the Mumbai High Court gave an order in favour of Air India based on
certain assurances given by the Management relating to service conditions, continuity of service
and protection of employees’ pay and benefits. The Unions then filed an SLP before the Supreme
Court. Who has also decided in favour of Air India on 9
th May, 2013. Further steps towards
operationalisition will now be taken. However, a section of employees have also approached the
Chennai High Court challenging the transfer of employees to the Ground Handling Company. As a
result of implementation of the Charamadhikari Committee Report, the revised CTC i.e. cost to the
company has been determined. The new CTC will be implemented as per the DPE norms and scale.
As regards licensed categories the Cabinet has given its approval to rationalize the pay structures
in line with the competition.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
28. The Committee notes the reply and feels that the employees related issues of
subsidiaries of Air India should be addressed at the earliest. In this regard the Committee
reiterates its recommendation that these outstanding issues must be settled as early as
possible to enable Air India function as a single entity.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
29. The Committee further recommends that before taking any policy decision in respect of AI,
proper study and analysis of its impact on the functioning and viability of Air India should be
carried out. Air India is our national carrier in which thousands of crores of rupees of taxpayers’
money has been invested. The Committee, therefore, calls upon the Ministry and AI to keep this
fact always in mind while taking any decision.
(Para 41 of ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
30. Government is aware of the huge infusion being made towards the Financial Restructuring
Plan and Turn Around Plan of Air India. Several cost control measures have been initiated during
the last couple of years in order to improve Air India’s operational and financial performance. The
cash losses came down in 2012-13 as compared to 2011-12. No fresh recruitment has taken place
in Air India for the last several years. Old and ageing aircraft have been grounded and are being
disposed of and new state of the art aircraft are being inducted in the fleet in order to improve
the schedule integrity and reduce the maintenance cost. Similarly, new routes which are being

6
planned taken into account the cash margins which can be generated on these routes. The working
capital loans have been restructured to reduce interest cost. PLI has been abolished with effect
from 1 st July, 2012 and the pay structure has been rationalized.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
31. The Committee feels that with a committed annual Government equity, Air India can
improve its performance more than the parameters mentioned in TAP in the coming years and
reaffirm its status of ‘Maharaja’.
(Para 42 of ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
32. To achieve a cash positive status by the year 2016 and PAT (Profit after Tax) positive
status by 2018, every effort is being made in order to achieve these parameters under the TAP.
Due to the induction of new aircraft in its fleet, the average age of the fleet is less than 5 years.
Air India is confident of regaining the status of ‘Maharaja’ in the coming years.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
33. The Committee notes the reply and hopes that measures taken under the Turn
Around Plan of Air India and induction of new aircraft in its fleet will help the national
carrier to regain its numero uno  status.
HOTEL CORPORATION OF INDIA
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE

timeframe.
(Para 47 of ibid)

35. Funds of Rs.10.00 crores in Financial Year 2012-13 to be utilized by Hotel Corporation of

Financial Year (2013-14) and additional fund allocation may be considered later.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
36. The Committee feels that the Ministry of Civil Aviation should take up its case with
Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission for further allocation of funds for the Hotel

AIRPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
37. The Committee finds that the AAI was allocated a budgetary support of Rs.280 crores (BE)
for the year 2012-13 while it has been reduced to Rs.42.00 crores in BE 2013-14. Out of this,

(Para 61 of ibid)

38. AAI has sought additional grants of Rs.462.21 crore in 2013-14 at RE-2013-14 stage. The

39. AAI has also informed that it will submit a proposal soon for release of balance fund for
GAGAN Project to the Ministry.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
40. The Committee notes the reply and observes that enhancement of grant for AAI for its
projects in North Eastern Region at RE stage will strengthen the airport infrastructure in NER.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
41. The Committee also finds that out of the required 3500 ATCs to control the Indian skies
only 2300 personnel are available. The Committee hopes that AAI will take necessary steps to
address the issue by augmenting its training facilities at Allahabad.
(Para 62 of ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
42. The AAI Board has approved the creation of 1200 posts Junior Executive (ATC).
Recruitment of 200 Junior Executive (ATC) is proposed to be undertaken every six months. AAI
has also informed that the training facilities at Allahabad, Hyderabad and Gondia training centres
have already been adequately augemented.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
43. The Committee is happy to note that large number of posts have been created as JE
(ATC), recruitment is on and training facilities have been augmented at designated places
on the basis of its recommendations.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
44. The Committee was informed on the deadlock persisting over the development of Patna

8
airport. The Committee reiterates its observation/recommendation contained in its 174 th Report in
respect of Patna Airport last year and hopes that the AAI will pursue the matter with the State
Government of Bihar for ensuring some viable alternate plan taking into consideration impending
danger for the air travelers to Patna. The Committee would like to have a status note including
efforts made, alternate proposals and the results thereof.
(Para 63 of ibid)
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
45. Government of Bihar vide letter dated 19.01.2011 and 14.10.2011 had requested AAI to
construct a Greenfield Airport at Nalanda with 1200 acres of land to be provided by State
Government. AAI vide letter dated 4.01.2012 has conveyed to the Government of Bihar may
develop a Greenfield Airport at Nalanda under PPP mode subject to mandatory clearances,
applicable rules and regulations.
46. AAI has informed Chief Secretary, Government of Bihar vide letter dated 21.02.2012 that
there is no possibility of upgrading the runway at Patna airport due to non-availability of land and
presence of obstacles in both directions of runway. On the request of State Govt., AAI had carried
out a feasibility study for a Greenfield airport at Nalanda and for construction of civil enclave and
extension of existing runway upto 3800 m at Bihta. The study report was submitted to State Govt.
of Bihar and AAU has proposed 4800 acres of land as recommended in the feasibility study for
developing Greenfield at Nalanda but the State Government has offered 1200 acres only. Apart from
identifying and acquiring extent of land needed, the establishement of physical facilities on the land
is another issue, which may cost anywhere around Rs.1000-1200 crores approx for Phase 1 (for
A320 type operations) development. Bihta Airport belonging to IAF can be considered as an
aternative to Patna airport for wide bodied airport operations and for establishment of Civil
Enclave, as basic infrastructure including runway already exist. At Bihta airport, extension of
runway of dimensions 3800 x 45m suitable for wide bodied aircraft with Cat-1 approach lights is
possible.
47. AAI had submitted concept proposal for the development of Civil Aviation in the state of
Bihar and accordingly, the Ministry of Civil Aviation has taken up the matter with the Ministry of
Defence. It has been proposed that AAI airport at Gaya may be exchanged with IAF’s Bihta Airport
which is a fully developed airport in the vicinity of Patna. It is proposed to retain 78 acres of land
together with existing terminal at Gaya airport with AAI as civil enclave for operating civil flights.
Given the proximity of Bihta to Patna, the Bihta airport after development would be able to service
the civil aviation requirements of Patna city.
48. Secretary, Civil Aviation has also written to the Government of Bihar to consider the option
of swapping the Bihta airstrip with Gaya airport and to convey the concurrence of the State
Government to it so that the matter could be taken up with the Ministry of Defence.
49. Response of State Government is awaited.
50. As regards to existing Patna airport, all the obstacles (trees) in the approach path of runway
are pruned and licensing of airport is under examination.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
51. The Committee has been expressing its concern about Patna airport and hopes that
the coordinated efforts between Ministries of Civil Aviation, Defence and State Government
of Bihar will definitely end the stalemate over development of airport in Bihta as an
alternative to Patna airport.

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
72. While assessment of traffic potential, future growth, demand-supply gap, load factors
are criteria generally adopted for deciding bilateral traffic rights, there are other vital
considerations such as requirements projected by the eligible airlines of India for foreign
operations, enhancement of international connectivity, geo political, economic, diplomatic or
strategic considerations and overall passenger interests which are taken into account while
entering into bilateral air services negotiations. The bilateral air services negotiations with UAE
(Abu Dhabi) were held in view of demands from Abu Dhabi as well as Indian carriers,
passengers interests for enhanced international connectivity to new overseas destinations and
services from international airports in India other than gateway cities besides overall economic
interest of India in terms of Government’s policy of liberatlisation for attracting foreign
investment in various sector including civil aviation. The MOU signed with Abu Dhabi extends
benefits to Indian carriers such as fifth freedom rights both intermediate and beyond points
with change in guauge facility at Abu Dhabi which will facilitate optimal utilization of aircraft
resources and providing enhanced connectivity. Adequately safeguards have been built in the
MOU to protect the interest of Indian carriers/airport operators. The enhancement in traffic
entitlements has been done in a phased manner with sector specific capping, limiting the
operational flexibility of the foreign carrier and providing adequate time to Indian carriers to
plan and consolidate their position to keep pace with growing Indian aviation market. Further,
stakeholder consultation is invariably done prior to bilateral negotiations and views of all the
stakeholders including the national carrier is taken into account by inter-ministerial group
comprising of representatives from various ministries/departments to decide the negotiating
strategy and mandate for the negotiating team. The recent negotiations in respect of India-Abu
Dhabi air services matters was done as per the mandate given by a Group of Ministers. The
bilateral traffic rights to Indian carriers are allocated as per laid down guidelines. However,
primacy of the national carrier has been retained as traffic rights are allocated to other carriers
only after considering the operational requirements of Air India.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the
observations/recommendations as contained in its One-Hundred and Eighty-Eighth Report on
“Functioning of Commission of Railways Safety” which was presented to both the Houses of
Parliament on 27
th February, 2013.
2. The Ministry of Civil Aviation submitted the interim Action Taken Replies on 7 th October,
2013 and the final Action Taken Replies on 22 nd January, 2014 containing the views of Ministry
of Railways also. The Committee heard the views of the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Railway
Board on the Action Taken Replies in its meeting held on 27
th January, 2014. The observations/
recommendations contained in the Report have been categorized as follows:—
(i) Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry:
Para Nos. 23, 56, 57, 84, 85, 86, 96 and 97
(ii) Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in
view of the Ministry replies:
Para Nos. 57, 58, 73, 85, 87 and 97
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Ministry have not
been accepted by the Committee:
Para Nos. 16, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 55, 56, 59, 71, 72, 84 and 98
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Ministry are
still awaited:
Para Nos. 8, 17, 18, 42, 48, 49, 50, 76, 77 and 94
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which
have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the
earliest.
4. On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each
item of Action taken/proposed to be taken by the concerned Ministries. The recommendations of
the Committee contained in the One Hundred and Eighty Eighth Report, action taken/views thereon
by the Ministries of Civil Aviation and Railways and further recommendations/observations of the
Committee on each item of action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
5. However, after the first round of discussions with the both the Ministries separately and
also with the CCRS, the Committee found that the two Ministries had quite different, sometimes
opposite views on certain crucial issues relating to effectiveness, autonomy and need to empower
and restructure the CRS. The Ministry of Railways maintained that the CRS was fulfilling its
mandate effectively and had enjoyed complete autonomy and that its views are taken quite seriously
and most of its recommendations are implemented and that there was no need to disturb the
existing arrangement to further restructure/empower CRS. The Ministry of Civil Aviation which is
also Central Government for the CRS had expressed contrary views on many such issues.
(Para No. 8 of 188
th Report)

2
REPLY FROM M/O RAILWAYS
6. Noted. It is reiterated that the existing institution of the Commission of Railway Safety
under the Ministry of Civil Aviation is working satisfactorily. There is no interference from the
Ministry of Railways in the functioning of the Commission.
STAND OF MINISTRY OF CIVIL A VIATION
7. Effectiveness of Commission of Railway Safety is much below the required level as present
set up is such that Commissioners have to rely on facilities extended by Railways. Chief
Commissioner of Railway Safety is of the opinion that Commission of Railway Safety needs to be
restructured, with a view to strengthen the organization, so as to improve its efficiency and
effectiveness, with least reliance on Railways for technical and logistic support.
ACTION TAKEN
8. A proposal to appoint consultant to examine the present functioning of the CRS with a view
to suggest reforms for augmentation, strengthening and restructuring the organization so as to
improve its efficiency and effectiveness is under active consideration with Ministry of Civil
Aviation. Subsequent action shall be initiated after submission of the report by the consultant.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
9. The Committee observes that the replies submitted by both the Ministries of Civil
Aviation and Railways are divergent and diagonally opposite. The Committee strongly feels
that it is high time that both the Ministries sorted out their differences on crucial issues
related to CRS. The Committee is pleased to note that a proposal to appoint consultant to
examine the present functioning of CRS is under active consideration of the Ministry of
Civil Aviation. The Committee desires that urgent steps should be taken to finalize the
proposal and implement the same.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
DUALITY OF COMMAND
10. Thus, CRS functions under Rules framed by both the Ministries under the Railways Act.
While accident investigation related rules are issued by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, accidents
inquiry related rules were issued by the Ministry of Railways. Though the CRS is under the
administrative control of Ministry of Civil Aviation, it takes its origin and discharges its duties as
per the Rules and Regulations framed under the Railways Act. The Committee feels that
involvement of two Ministries - Ministry of Railways and Ministry of Civil Aviation, leads to
avoidable confusion and also makes it difficult to apportion the responsibilities due to duality of
control and command in the functioning of CRS. It also leaves scope for conflict of interest for
Ministry of Railways.
(Para No: 16 ibid)
REPLY FROM M/O RAILWAYS
11. As far as the Ministry of Railways is concerned, there is no confusion in functioning of
the Commission of Railway Safety under the Ministry of Civil Aviation even when it takes its origin
and discharges its duties under the Railways Act 1989 as the duties and powers of both Ministry
of Railways and the CRS are well defined. Whenever any dispute arises in respect of any aspect
of the functioning of the Commissioner of Railway Safety (CRS), it is resolved by both the

3
Ministries mutually within the framework of the Act. Ministry of Railways and the Commission of
Railway Safety under the Ministry of Civil Aviation are Government bodies functioning in the public
interest and carrying out their respective duties as defined in the Act. There is no interference or
exercising of influence on the part of the Ministry of Railways in the working of the Commission.
Commissioners of Railway Safety are completely independent and exercise their independent and
free judgment while discharging their duties under the Act.
STAND OF MINISTRY OF CIVIL A VIATION
12. Commissioners of Railway Safety are concerned with the safety control aspects of the
operations of the railways, whereas Ministry of Railways plays the role of operator and regulator
both. There have been instances when Railway Board has not kept balance between its role as
operator vis-a-vis role of regulator.
13. Unilaterally changing of rules, schedule of dimensions and manuals etc. by the Ministry of
Railways without the concurrence of MoCA (administrative ministry in r/o CRS) has been a cause
of concern for the CRS. Such actions lead to lowering/compromising with the desired safety
standards. Further such action on the part of Railways leads to confusion/differences between the
two organizations. The issue is to be addressed on priority basis.
ACTION TAKEN
14. Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation vide its DO letter dated 08.08.2013 to Railway Board,
has proposed to formalize the process of fixing minimum requirements/standards ( e.g. Schedule of
Dimensions, Standards for fixed Structures and rolling Stocks and Rules governing Train
operations) which regulate railway Safety.
15. In response to Secretary MOCA letter, Ministry of Railways have withstood with their
earlier reply and opined that for changing the rules and Standards it is not obligatory to consult
the Commission of Railway Safety as per statute.
16. No conclusive decision reached due to stand of the Ministry of Railways as conveyed
above.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
17. The Committee feels that stand taken by the Ministry of Civil Aviation as well as
the Railways do not address the concerns of the Committee on the duality of command in
discharging the functions of CRS. The Committee is of the considered view that having a
separate legislation for CRS, which could prove to be an effective solution to such avoidable
confusion, needs serious thought and deliberation.
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
18. Besides, under the Railways Act the term Central Government means the Ministry of
Railways. There being some overlapping in safety related issues between the Railway Board and
CRS as it is, this confusion gets further confounded. Although Ministry of Railways denied the
existence of such confusion, instances of unilateral action by the Railway Board for deciding
standards and codes and informing the Commission of Railway Safety without any involvement/
consultation with the latter were brought to the notice of the Committee. The Committee is
constrained to conclude that such an arrangement is suitable to Ministry of Railways which is why
it does not want to disturb the existing arrangement.
(Para No: 17 ibid)

4
REPLY FROM M/O RAILWAYS
19. As per Section 60 of Indian Railways Act, the power to make rules for regulating the
traveling upon, and the use, working and management of Railways lies with Central Government
i.e. Ministry of Railways. The Commission of Railway Safety has to discharge its duties within the
framework of rules formulated by Ministry of Railways.
20. As per statute it is not obligatory to consult the Commission before any amendment/
revision/deletion/addition to General Rules and other Rules, standards, codes and manuals.
STAND OF MINISTRY OF CIVIL A VIATION
21. As per the transaction of Business Rules – when the subject of a case concerns more than
one department, no decision can be taken or order issued until all such departments have
concurred, or, failing such concurrence, a decision thereon has been taken by or under the
authority of the Cabinet.
The stand of the Railways that the Commission of Railway Safety has to discharge its
duties within the framework of rules formulated by the Ministry of Railways is legally incorrect.
Commissioners of Railway Safety have been bestowed responsibility and powers by the Act of
Parliament, to inspect/inquire/investigate and then to report on safety related issues to Government.
Section 60 of the Indian Railways Act, 1989 as referred to by the Ministry of Railways mentions
about the carriage of passengers rules only and not on operation. Operational rules are actually the
subject matter under Section 29(2)(c) of the Railways Act.
22. Section 29 is reproduced below:

66. The argument extended by the Ministry of Railways in respect of its order issued in the
year 1953 relieving CsRS of their duty of ‘annual periodical inspection’ is not legally tenable. The

duty of inspection provided to the Commissioners by the Act of 1890. This amounts to by-passing
the law making power of Parliament. Besides, the Committee does not agree with the Ministry’s
argument that this was done under the power to issue direction by the Central Government, as
provided in Section 6(b) of the Railways Act. The Committee is of the view that the power to issue
directions given to the Ministry by the Act, cannot be used to take away something given by the
same Act. This is against the basic tenets of subordinate legislation. This ‘power to issue direction’
should relate to such details, procedures, manner, formalities, timings, etc. of the inspection and
certainly not for withdrawing these powers. And the Ministry is supposed to have laid down rules,
etc. for carrying out these functions. The Committee does not know if any rule, regulations etc.
have been framed under this.

Order became inoperative with the new Railway Act coming into being in 1989, the Ministry of
Railways should have issued a fresh circular clarifying the position, which unfortunately was not
done. In the absence of such a clarification, the said Order continued to remain in operation till

to be settled on priority in consultation with the Ministry of Law and Justice under intimation
to this Committee.
