RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATION   OF THE COMMITTEE

connectivity to 24 airports in the country for arou nd 15 km area around each airport at an 
estimated cost of Rs.5 crore per kilometre. The Com mittee would like to know the progress 
made in the project how much fund so far allocated for this scheme, which airport has been 
linked with good roads, and by when all the propose d 24 airports will be linked with good 
roads. 
(Para 122 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government 
 
226. Various new schemes were proposed to be taken up during the twelfth Five Year Plan 
(2012-17). These included proposal for taking up Sp ecial package for development of road 
connectivity for 24 Airports involving 360 km for total GBS requirement of Rs. 1,800 crore. 
227. However, in the absence of additional budgetar y supports, the same could not be 
taken up so far.

RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE  
7. The Committee notes from this table two trends –  (i) there has been only 
marginal increments in the GBS to the Ministry ever y year and (ii) this GBS has been 
invariably reduced at RE stage every year. Taking a  realistic view, if expenditure is 
taken in terms of RE allocation, its percentage has  been satisfactory and as per the 
financial norms. It means that Ministry has shown its capability to spend the finds given 
to it every year. The Committee, however, fails to understand, how the Ministry of 
Finance could with such a good expenditure, allocat e funds to Ministry of Shipping 
with a marginal increase every year. In other words , may be, if it is given more funds 
which shipping sector needs badly, the Ministry cou ld have fruitfully used it. The 
Committee in view of the potential and capabilities  of Shipping sector in our economy 
in days to come, recommends that Ministry of Financ e must increase GBS to Ministry 
of Shipping every year substantially.  
 (Recommendation at Para No. 7 of 235 th  Report) 
Reply of the Government  
8. Continuous efforts are made to seek additionalit y from Ministry of Finance by 
this Ministry.

9. The Committee notes the reply.

10. The Committee further observes that the non-pla n expenditure is also has been 
good showing above 95% spending during the last 4 y ears except during 2013-14 
which was 85.86% of the RE.  
 (Para No. 8 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government 
 
11. Noted. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE  
12. The Committee notes the reply. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE  
13. The Committee further observes that the IEBR gr oss expenditure stands only at 
59.35% which also steadily decreased in the first t hree years. As in the case of Plan 
allocation IEBR has also shown improvement during 2 015-16. But, still more needs to 
be done.  

(Para No. 9 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
14. In so far as Port Wing is concerned, the IEBR o utlays for the Major Ports in 
Annual Plans 2012-13 to 2015-16 have been as under:

15. The gross actual utilization of the IEBR during  the years 2013-14, 2014-15 and 
2015-16 with reference to BE allocations has been 7 1.82%, 68.24% and 86.92% 
respectively. The observations of the Committee hav e been noted for further 
improvement.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
16. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee re commends further that 
Major Ports may implement its modernization works using the IEBR Funds as far 
as possible so that capacity addition works could be completed as per schedule. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION  OF THE COMMITTEE 
17. In the case of IEBR Committee notes that it has  registered consistent decline 
from 2013-14 on words. Similarly, IEBR were reduced each year, except in 2012-13, at 
RE stage; reduction being about 35 to 40%. Needless  to add, expenditure of IEBR also 
had declined and its percentage was not as good as in the case of GBS. Such a negative 
variation in case of IEBR shows that the performanc e of our ports and shipping sector 
need to be examined to find out real reasons for de cline in generation of internal 
resources/revenue. While good expenditure of GBS ma y indicates good performance, 
declining IEBR generation tells opposite story. The  Committee would like to know 
reasons for this and recommends the Ministry of Shi pping make all out efforts for 
correcting this situation as shipping sector is goi ng to face tremendous challenge in 
coming days.  
(Para No. 10 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government 
 
18. The observations of the Committee have been not ed in the Port Wing. 
Utilisation of IEBR by some of the Major Ports with  reference to BE allocations during 
the years 2012-13 to 2015-16 has been low. A few of  the broad reasons for the low 
utilization have been restructuring/ refiguring of some projects/schemes, lack of 
response against bids, delays in CRZ/MOEF clearance s, litigation etc. The Ports are 
repeatedly being advised at various forums to ensur e maximum utilization of the IEBR 
allocations. Utilisation of IEBR allocated to the M ajor Ports under Annual Plan 2016-
17 has been included as a key activity in the Actio n Plan of the Ministry 2016-17 and 
being regularly monitored at various levels. IEBR a llocation to the Major Ports under 
Annual Plan 2016-17 is Rs. 1832.09 crore and it would be the endeavour of the Ports to 
expend the amount fully. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
19. The Committee notes the reply and hopes that ex penditure pattern under 
IEBR will be improved after the efforts made by the Ministry. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 

20. The Committee observes that during 2015-16, whi le the BE was Rs.932.79, the 
RE stands at Rs.824.00 which shows that there was n ot any major cut for the Ministry 
last year. Even some sectors like Ports and ALHW go t enhanced allocations, during 
2015-16.  
(Para No. 13 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government  
21. Noted 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
22.  The Committee notes the reply. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
23. The Committee further observes that during 2015 -16, the Ministry of Finance 
did not allocate the additional amount sought at th e RE stage. The Committee, 
however, recommends that higher allocations at RE s tage may be allowed during the 
current financial year so that the Ministry of Ship ping may make up the back log in 
their completion of projects already undertaken in previous years.  
(Para No. 14 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government 
 
24. Continuous efforts are made to seek additionali ty from Ministry of Finance by 
this Ministry.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
25. The Committee notes the reply. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
26. The Committee observes that compared to 2015-16 , the allocation in 2016- 17 
for the Major Ports have been highly insufficient. As per the projection made by the 
Ministry, they demanded Rs.467.48 crore whereas the  allocation is a very meager 
amount of Rs.29.01 crore, which will adversely affe ct the modernization/capacity 
enhancement projects of the Tuticorin, Chennai and Mormugao Ports. The Committee 
recommends that additional allocation for the ports may be made at RE Stage.  
(Para No. 18 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government 
 
27. The observations of the Committee have been not ed for seeking appropriate 
allocations for the Ports at RE Stage. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
28. The Committee further recommends that sufficient al locations may be 
made to major ports. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
29. The Committee further observes that the IWT Sec tor is a very important and 
emerging Sector which will be able to generate suff icient cargo and passenger 
movement in a very economical manner compared to ot her modes of transport. In such 
a scenario, allocating only Rs.350.00 crore where d emand stands at Rs.2384.00 crore is 
not helping the IWT Sector in a big way. The Commit tee also understands that the Jal 
Marg Vikas project will be affected due to insuffic ient allocation. The Committee 
recommends for more allocation for the IWT Sector.    
(Para No. 19 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government 
 
30. It is true that IWT Sector is a growing sector which needs sufficient funds for 
development and maintenance in respect of 111 Natio nal Waterways (NWs) under The 
National Waterways Act, 2016.  Development of these  NWs for shipping and 
commercial navigation in a phased manner requires s ustainable source of funding as 
existing Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) of Rs. 350.0 0 crore in Budget Estimate-2016-

17 is grossly inadequate.   In addition, as per announcement made in the Budget Speech 
on 29 th  February, 2016, Inland Waterways Authority of Indi a (IWAI) has initiated 
action for raising Bonds worth Rs. 1000 crore durin g the current fiscal year (2016-17) 
in two tranches (December, 2016 & March, 2017) for funding development of NWs. 
31.         Funding support by multi-lateral instit ution and wherever feasible, by forming 
Joint Ventures (JVs) with Private/ Public Companies , State Governments and Ports for 
specific projects are alternative sources which wou ld be tapped by IWAI on case to 
case basis.   
32.        Meanwhile, an appropriate option for funding NWs is to earmark 5% of Central 
Road Funds (CRF) for development of NWs in the coun try by amending the Central 
Road Fund Act, 2000 appropriately.    Ministry of S hipping is preparing a Draft Note 
for Cabinet in this regard. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
33. The Committee notes the reply. The Committee de sires to know the 
outcome of the steps taken by the Ministry in getti ng enhanced allocations for the 
IWT Sector and the Governments response in this matter. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
34. The Committee understands that the Ministry of Shipping has completed 
preparatory project development work related to por t modernization; coastal shipping, 
coastal berths, IWT and ALHW, which needs additiona l funds for completion of the 
projects. The Committee recommends that the Ministr y of Finance may look into the 
matter in view of the importance of the infrastruct ure development in the Port and 
Shipping Sectors; and sufficient funds may be allocated for these projects this year.  
(Para No. 20 of ibid )

39. File has been processed for increasing the Plan  Fund allocation to IMU during

increasing the Plan Fund allocation.  The proposal will be taken up with Ministry of 
Finance at Supplementary Stage. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
40.  The Committee notes the reply and desires to know the outcome thereof. 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
41. The Committee takes a serious view of the fact that the amount allocated for the 
Major Ports are very insignificant compared to the role and importance of the ports in 
earning revenue for the country and generating employment on large scale. Many of the 
Major Ports have not got any allocation this year a nd some ports have got very 
negligible amount. Many important projects of the M ajor Ports as mentioned by the 
Ministry of Shipping have been kept aside due to no n-allocation of funds. The 
Committee notes that the Ports Sector has been allo cated only Rs. 29 crore wherein 
various Major Ports require additional fund of Rs. 388.61 core for meeting the 
commitments made by them during 2016-17. The Commit tee recommends that 
sufficient fund allocations may be made to the Majo r Ports at the RE stage so that they 
can complete the ongoing projects and the projects to be undertaken during 2016-17.  
(Para No. 26 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government 
 
42. Observations of the Committee have been noted a nd additional funds would be 
sought at RE Stage. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
43.  The Committee notes the reply. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
44. The Committee appreciates the Major Ports like Kolkata, Paradip, Kamarajar, 
V.O. Chidambaranar, Cochin, Mormugao, Jawaharlal Ne hru and Kandla have shown 
positive growth during 2015-16. The Committee observes that even though 8 ports have 
made positive growth but four major ports have made  negative figures in cargo 
handling during this period.  
(Para No. 30 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government 
 
45. Observations of the Committee are noted. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 

46. The Committee desires to know the steps taken to improve the 
performance of the ports during the current Financial Year. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
47. The Committee notes that ICTT Vallarpadam has s hown some improvement in 
the container handling during 2015-16 with the effo rts of the Cochin Port Trust. The 
Committee desires that extensive measures are furth er required to make the ICTT an 
important destination for cargo handling. The Committee also of the view that vigorous 
marketing of the Vallarpadam Terminal at the indust rial hubs of the neighboring States 
need to be done and special tariff and smooth conta iner transportation facilities should 
be provided for further improvement of the cargo traffic at Vallarpadam. 
(Para No. 31 of ibid ) 
Reply of the Government 
 
48. Cochin Port Trust has taken a number of initiat ives for increasing container 
handling at ICTT.  Some of the major initiatives are: 
(i) A dedicated rail service is in operation from Coimb atore from 16.01.2016.  
The CoPT  has entered into an MoU with CONCOR to ru n one rake per 
week on a fixed day for 6 months between Coimbatore  and Cochin 
irrespective of Volumes, with CoPT guaranteeing a m inimum of 80 laden 
TEUs for a two way trip. 
(ii) Procedures streamlined at the interstate check post  at Walayar.  The 
Government of Kerala has instituted a Green Channel  at Walayar Check 
Post to speed up the clearance of export containers  which is fully 
operational from 05.01.2016. 
(iii) Regular trade meetings have been conducted at Tirup ur & Pollachi and 
bottlenecks cleared for container movement.  This h as resulted in growth of 
14.5% in container handling during 2015-16.  The po rt is pursuing more
